messages:
Elena R: Kicking off canary v2026-07-20 -> 5% across eu-west-1 per change window. Watching p95 and embedding quality for 10m quiet.
Marco: I'll monitor infra and routing. Call stop if p95 > 3x or embedding drift > 3%.
ops-bot: ALERT: canary-eu-west p95 jumped 115ms -> 490ms at T+6m. 5xx stable.
Priya S: Traces point to two instances with repeated syscalls blocking (eu1-host-11, eu1-host-12). KV eviction spike also visible.
Elena R: OK. Prefer routing override to avoid full rollback. If routing-change doesn't stabilize within 8m we rollback to v2026-07-12. Agreed?
Marco: Agreed. Also spin a short autoscale buffer (+20%) to smooth transient misses.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: action request: route-override apply --selector canary:v2026-07-20 --exclude-hosts eu1-host-11,eu1-host-12 --until 5012349000 --reason "noisy-host-syscall"
deploy-bot: status: routing job rchg-14107 started
ops-bot: INFO: rchg-14107 progress: 2/3 updated, 1 retry pending
Marco: One instance hit a socket timeout applying the override; retrying now.
deploy-bot: status: rchg-14107 completed at 5012346958: 3/3 success
Marco: p95 back to ~135ms after routing change. KV evictions trending down. No increase in 5xx.
Elena R: Great. Extend canary observation by 25m and annotate release notes: "Extended canary hold (+25m) due to transient host syscall stalls in eu-west-1; routing override applied; no rollback."
Priya S: Opening INC-7890 to drain/reprovision eu1-host-11/12 and mark them for maintenance.
qa-bot: QA: quick quality checks running on latest canary logs; no embedding regressions observed so far.
Elena R: We'll resume the slow ramp after the extended window. If we see recurrence we'll either pin region or perform a rollback. For now, no rollback required. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: NOTE: canary hold extended until 5012348500 per change update.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: rchg-14107 completed successfully.
Marco: I'll follow up with infra to schedule reprovision and link INC-7890 to maintenance calendar.
Elena R: Closing thread for now. Reopen if any new anomalies pop up."
